docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode" (a wait only a command's peer can end is refused in sim): a command runs on the baton under a real-time bound, block= (2 s by default), and any command slower than it is refused, whether it waits on another activity or is only slow; timing-dependent by nature, and block= is how a program with slow commands runs under sim

docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode" (a wait only a native's own thread or a peer can end is refused in sim): a native call that leaves its driver runs on the baton under block=, past which the interpreter's thread is signalled once and the call refused once it returns; any such call slower than the bound is refused, timing-dependent by nature; a native that retries on EINTR or blocks outside a system call stays unbounded, and so does a native call under a pin, which does not leave its driver (it hangs on the oracle too)
docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode": a deadlock in the simulation mode is a loud refusal; virtual time cannot end a wait only a real signal can

docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode": any inbox post other than a signal's halt, and a callback from a thread running none of the interpreter's native calls, is a determinism breach, refused loudly

docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode" (trace and replay): a replay takes the trace's decisions in order, and one the run takes otherwise (another program, a damaged or edited file) is refused rather than run on a schedule the trace does not hold
docs/design/architecture.md, "Simulation mode" (trace and replay): a run asked for a decision trace that it cannot write fails, so a harness that checks the status learns it has none
